refs.q: *zebra* is an IP routing manager. It provides kernel routing table updates, interface lookups, and redistribution of routes between different routing protocols.

atoms.tpl: Context: zebra is an IP routing manager providing kernel routing table updates, interface lookups, and redistribution of routes between different routing protocols.

refs.q: Specify which kernel routing table *Zebra* should communicate with.

atoms.tpl: Decision: zebra is the process that communicates with the kernel routing tables — protocol daemons interact only through ZAPI requests and notifications.
Consequence: zebra implements the frr-zebra northbound model with 164 YANG paths and 6 YANG paths on frr-zebra-route-map, served by 183 NB handler tables.
Consequence: zebra is the ZAPI server — it handles 94 message types published by the route daemons and emits 44 notification/event types back to clients.
Provenance: decision statements are authored from FRR documentation; quotes are validated verbatim by the verifier, consequences are measured graph facts.
